FIB_PLUS	<p>17c5_8114</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6f42ab;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ekm, +++, ekm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>350b_c028</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266e37;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #266e37;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266e37;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6f42ab;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hmp, +++, hmp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3140;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9f3140;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3140;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c690f;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4c690f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c690f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4fb9;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4c4fb9;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c4fb9;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bhr, +++, bhr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. genes and assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul> <li>Step 5: Go back to Step 2 and pick a new pair of genes until all pairs are Finding a decimal in your answer, such as 5.5, indicates a mistake was made. Please provide your answer as a complete number without fractions or decimals.</li><li><i>Important Tip 2:</i> Your answer should be written as a numerical value only, with no spaces, commas, or units such as "cM" or "map units". The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #266e37;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #266e37;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266e37;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #285ea5;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #285ea5;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #285ea5;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2e6b;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9a2e6b;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>6cf5_efa7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993e1b;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #993e1b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993e1b;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #016e55;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #016e55;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #016e55;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6f42ab;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, krw, +++, krw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #78580e;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #78580e;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #78580e;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #016e55;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #016e55;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #016e55;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2e6b;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9a2e6b;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2e6b;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dew, +++, dew"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>dda2_7ead</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993e1b;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #993e1b;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993e1b;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6879;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1b6879;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6879;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6f42ab;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266e37;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #266e37;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266e37;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #285ea5;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #285ea5;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #285ea5;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bmt, +++, bmt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3140;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9f3140;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3140;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c690f;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4c690f;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c690f;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4fb9;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4c4fb9;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c4fb9;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fkt, +++, fkt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>edb6_252e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #78580e;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #78580e;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #78580e;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4fb9;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4c4fb9;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>b882_d8bc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676016;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #676016;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676016;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #285ea5;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #285ea5;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #285ea5;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2e6b;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9a2e6b;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2e6b;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fhr, +++, fhr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>b05d_1ec4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266e37;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #266e37;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266e37;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3194;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8b3194;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993e1b;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #993e1b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993e1b;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c690f;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4c690f;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c690f;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6f42ab;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kty, +++, kty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #78580e;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #78580e;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #78580e;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #016e55;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #016e55;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #016e55;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2e6b;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9a2e6b;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9a2e6b;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ekr, +++, ekr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>003e_3910</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3194;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8b3194;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3194;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hmx, +++, hmx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>6460_3885</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3140;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9f3140;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3140;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c690f;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4c690f;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c690f;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cdr, +++, cdr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>dce6_165c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993e1b;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #993e1b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993e1b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c690f;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4c690f;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4c690f;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #285ea5;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #285ea5;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>0ed9_0493</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676016;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #676016;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676016;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4fb9;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4c4fb9;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>4cfa_6019</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #266e37;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #266e37;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266e37;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #285ea5;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #285ea5;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #285ea5;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2e6b;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9a2e6b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676016;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #676016;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676016;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6879;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1b6879;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6879;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3194;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8b3194;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3194;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cey, +++, cey"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>42f2_ce7d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #78580e;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #78580e;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #78580e;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #016e55;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #016e55;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #016e55;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4c4fb9;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4c4fb9;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>707b_4823</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #676016;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #676016;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #676016;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6879;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1b6879;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6879;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6f42ab;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, afr, +++, afr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #266e37;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #266e37;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266e37;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3194;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8b3194;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3194;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fhr, +++, fhr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>5950_fd14</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #78580e;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #78580e;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #78580e;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9a2e6b;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9a2e6b;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #993e1b;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #993e1b;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #993e1b;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #016e55;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #016e55;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #016e55;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6f42ab;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f42ab;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ahy, +++, ahy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9f3140;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9f3140;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f3140;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #266e37;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #266e37;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #266e37;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mpw, +++, mpw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
